images.seen: Africa: compiled map matches the period (Angola contested with UNITA and South African occupation hatched, Namibia under SA occupation, Western Sahara unowned after Spain, Zaire whole); small grey holes along some borders and a grey patch at Egypt's south-east corner (Halaib).

Middle East and South Asia: Iran, Afghanistan (mujahideen contest over the whole country, as the dossier draws it for Dec 1979), Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Burma look right; the grey Halaib hole at Egypt's south-east corner is still there; Sinai drawn as plain Egypt.
Levant before the patch: the whole Sinai is plain direct Egypt although Israel held it to 1982 (every partial occupation_end of the Egypt ledger closes the pair's whole occupation).
Western Sahara before the patch: a grey hole of 128 Smara cells; the Moroccan-held north drawn as plain SADR land; Mauritania's Tiris share and the Free Zone contest drawn as the dossiers intend.
Southeast Asia: compiled map right (Hainan with the PRC, unified Vietnam, Democratic Kampuchea, Indonesia with East Timor, PNG east of 141E); no speckle or jump.
After the patch: the Sinai east of the canal strip is hatched as Israeli-occupied, the Halaib cells are Sudan's, the Golan is occupied Syrian land.
After the patch: no grey hole; the Saguia el-Hamra is hatched as occupied by Morocco over the SADR claim, Tiris under Mauritania, Free Zone contested.

issues.what: Israel's occupation of the Sinai disappears from Oct 1973 to 1982: the Egypt ledger's occupation_end events of 1973, 1974 and 1975 release only the canal strip but the compiler closes the pair's whole occupation, so the Sinai (about 184 cells) is plain Egypt in 1973-1979.

Halaib Triangle: the Egypt dossier cuts 86 cells out of Egypt from 1971 (the 1973 keyframe snap removes 86) but no dossier gives them to Sudan, so they are owned by nobody from 1971 to 1994 and later.

Western Sahara 1976-79: 128 cells of the Saguia el-Hamra (Smara, filed by the gazetteer under Guelmim - Es-Semara) belong to no state after Spain leaves; the Moroccan-held north is drawn as plain SADR land because the dossier's own Morocco occupation_start is applied before the SADR keyframe exists.
Eritrea 1977: the EPLF 1977 keyframe cuts Barentu out of the EPLF's land but nothing gives it to Ethiopia, leaving 21 cells owned by nobody (the snap removed 26).

Seven cells of south Sakhalin, Tyuleniy Island and Iturup are still Japan's in the 1970 anchor; they are in conflict with the USSR in the published draft (Japan won as the smaller) and owned by Japan in the stage even after the conflict disappears.

Golan Heights: the seven Golan cells are owned by nobody in the 1970 anchor (the Ba'ath Party row's keyframe should hold them) and Israel's 1967 occupation of them is read the wrong way round, so 1970-72 is a hole and 1973-79 is plain Syria with no Israeli occupation.

Keyframe registration: Cliopatria shapes are about 1 cell off the gazetteer countries the dossiers' found events use; zaire_1971 (63 added, 114 removed, 37 kept by others), mozambique_1975 (72/69), people-s-republic-of-angola_1975 (21/55), papua-new-guinea_1976 (26/74, 15 cells of Indonesian Papua), republic-of-suriname_1975 (12 cells of Guyana), people-s-republic-of-bangladesh_1971, afghanistan_1978 (19 cells of Pakistan), islamic-republic-of-iran_1979 leave 60-100 unowned cells each inside the country and spill into neighbours; the same shape runs on to 2023.

Border conflicts where the smaller neighbour wins a few cells of the larger state (estado-novo/mozambique 72, zaire with zambia 19, uganda 15 and sudan 10, communist-laos/vietnam 21, india/burma 42, czechoslovakia/USSR 39, iraq/iran 18, afghanistan/tajik 30): all are border fuzz of one to three cells, no page dates or places them.

Afghanistan from 25 Dec 1979 is drawn contested with the mujahideen over the whole country (2281 cells) and the Soviet occupation has 0 cells; this is the dossiers' own reading ('Almost 80 percent of the country was outside government control').
Bophuthatswana (vassal_start of South Africa, 1977) is skipped: the gazetteer has no region of that name.

problems: The keyframe registration issue is systemic (see issues): each of these Cliopatria 'ok' keyframes runs to 2023, so a fix belongs to a global step (for example claiming the dossier's own found-event country region, or filling holes inside a state's own country) rather than 5-10 window patches; no keyframe_overrides were written.

events/3 (Sudan holds Halaib from 1970) reaches past the window: the cells stay Sudan's until the Egypt 2000 keyframe and Sudan's own 1994 contest_start; the p1990-p1999 and p2000-p2009 agents should expect Halaib to be Sudan's, not nobody's.
events/7 (seven Sakhalin and Kuril cells to the USSR from 1970) also removes the Japan/USSR conflict the p1990-p1999 ruling 1 addresses (1990-91); that ruling will then settle nothing.

events/5 (Morocco occupies the Saguia el-Hamra) and events/10 (Israel occupies the Golan from 1973) open occupations that stay open past 1979 until a dossier event closes them; the Golan one has no dossier end before 1981 and Quneitra's 1974 return to Syrian civil administration is not modelled (a few cells).

The published draft's Japan/USSR conflict (21 cell-years) and the new republic-of-poland/USSR conflict (18 cell-years) differ in the trial from other windows' patches or dossier edits made since 1 Nov 20:39, not from this patch.

South West Africa: the packet's 'occupation of south-africa's land by namibia' (2947 cells, 1966 to the end) names South Africa as owner and Namibia as occupier, which looks the wrong way round (South Africa occupied the territory); not checked against a page and not patched.

Greece 1974: greek-junta_1973 now shows a snap of 61 removed cells in the trial (not in the published packet); 11 Peloponnese and 11 Crete cells are unowned from the junta through the Third Republic; a Greek country-region keyframe would fill them.
